t: the months of the moon. The cycles of the moon.

as it is said, 'the burnt offering of each month in its month'. And it is interpreted as 'a month in its renewal' (see Targum Onkelos), that is, the lunar month, which depends on the moon's renewal (Ma'amar HaIbur).

and it says, 'This month shall be to you the head of months' etc.. This is another proof: from the word 'this' the Sages derived that the month is something visible to the eye, and from this the months written in the Torah are lunar months, which are visible (unlike the months of the solar year, which have no tangible expression).
the years of the sun. The length of time of the sun's cycle.

'Observe the month of Aviv'. The months of the year must be adjusted to the agricultural cycle so that the month of Nisan falls in the month during which the barley ripens (the 'aviv'), and this depends on the movement of the sun (see below 4:1).
the solar year. About 365 days.
the lunar year. Twelve lunar months, each month averaging about 29.5 days, in all about 354 days.
nearly eleven days. Approximately eleven days (the exact surplus is given below 6:4).

therefore when this surplus accumulates to about thirty days, they add one month. When the differences of several years accumulate to about thirty days, a month is added to the year, and thus the correspondence between the lunar months and the seasons of the year can be maintained.
an intercalated year. A year that has an addition (like a pregnant woman).

for it is impossible for the year to be twelve months and so many days etc.. From the phrase 'to the months of the year' we learn that the year is divided specifically into months and there is no possibility of adding a few days to the year; therefore one must wait until the difference between the solar and lunar years accumulates to a number of days close to a month, so that it can be completed with a whole month (and see below chapter 4).
and it is not seen for about two days etc.. The moon is not visible to the eye for about two days in every month.

about one day before it joins the sun at the end of the month, and about one day after it joins the sun. About a day before the end of the lunar cycle, when it passes in its orbit close to the sun and cannot be seen, and likewise about a day after the start of the cycle, when it is still impossible to see the moon (see the diagram on the next page).
and it will be seen in the west in the evening. The first sighting of the moon after it was hidden is on the western side at evening time.
and we do not need the moon. There is no need to see it.
an intercalated month. One that has an addition (like an intercalated year, above, halacha 2).
on the night of its intercalation. On the additional night of the month.
seeing the moon is not entrusted to every person. To determine on his own the day of Rosh Chodesh according to the sighting of the moon.
the Sabbath of Creation. The day of Shabbat; and each person can count six days from the previous Shabbat and rest.
the matter is entrusted to the court. The Great Court, the Sanhedrin (below 5:1; Sefer HaMitzvot, positive commandment 153).
until the court sanctifies it. By saying 'mekudash', as detailed below 2:8.
this testimony shall be entrusted to you. To Moses and Aaron, who throughout the generations are the Great Court of Israel (below 5:1).

they calculate with calculations. They calculate the courses of the heavenly bodies, according to the formulas received by tradition or according to the astronomers' calculations (see below 11:1-4, 17:24).
the astronomers. Scholars of astronomy.
and they investigate and examine closely. As detailed below from chapter 11 onward.
they sit and wait for witnesses. People who saw the new moon, on whose testimony the court sanctifies the month (see the next halacha).
and they have examined and investigated them according to halacha. As explained below 2:4-6.
and if it was not seen and no witnesses came. For example, if the viewing conditions did not allow it (below 18:1).

that they saw the image of a moon in the clouds. At the beginning of the month the moon is visible a little after sunset in the west, and its shape is a very thin illuminated band. Therefore thin clouds illuminated by the light of sunset may resemble the moon at its first appearance and can mislead witnesses (see below 2:6).
and they will send and inform. Through messengers or in another way, as below 3:8-14.
the rest of the people. Throughout the land and abroad.
on what day the festivals fall. On what day the holidays will fall, since the times of the festivals of that month are determined according to the time of Rosh Chodesh.

'And you shall keep this statute at its appointed time'. The statute of the festival of Passover must be observed at its time. And from these two verses we learn that there is an obligation to establish the festivals and publicize them, and for this the month must be sanctified.
that a person as great as he has arisen in the Land of Israel. That over time one of the sages of the Land of Israel became as great in wisdom as the man who went abroad.
except in the Land of Israel. As detailed below 5:1.

as it is said, 'For from Zion shall go forth Torah, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem'. The central authority for teaching in Israel has its place in the Land of Israel, whose capital is Jerusalem (and see below 4:12).
and was ordained in the Land of Israel. Ordained as a judge (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 4:1-3). And one cannot ordain outside the Land of Israel (ibid. 4:6).

two fit men who are qualified to testify in every matter. For the sanctification of the month is done before the Great Court, and its procedures are like the procedures of a trial (and see below 2:8).
but women and slaves are like the other persons disqualified from testimony. Although in certain matters they are believed to testify (see, for example, Hilchot Gerushin 12:15).
like the other persons disqualified from testimony. Those mentioned in Hilchot Edut 9:1 (and detailed in the following chapters there).
father and son. Who are disqualified from testifying together because of their kinship (ibid. 13:1).

that if one of them is found disqualified because he is a robber or other disqualification of the rest of the disqualifications, the second joins with another and testifies. We do not say that only one of them should go and join with another witness, lest the one who goes be disqualified, and it would turn out that the going of the witness who is his relative is needed too (see below, halacha 5).
and anyone disqualified from testimony by rabbinic enactment. For example, one who violated something prohibited by the Sages (Hilchot Edut 10:3).
for we are not strict with testimony about the month. Unlike other testimonies, in which one must scrutinize the witnesses carefully (Hilchot Edut 1:4).

zomemin. That other witnesses came and testified that the witnesses who testified about the birth of the moon could not have seen it at that time (ibid. 18:2); with another kind of testimony, their testimony would be void.
this is sanctified. For the court has the power to sanctify the month even if it was misled (below, halacha 10).

since the heretics corrupted. Who denied the tradition of the Oral Torah, and wished to cause the first day of Passover to fall on a Sunday so as to match the counting of the Omer to their halachic view (see Hilchot Temidin UMusafin 7:11).
and that they should investigate and examine his testimony. They scrutinize the details of the testimony to make sure the witnesses are not deceiving.
the court should not know the witnesses. They should not be acquainted with them.
who vouch for them to the court. They testify about them that they are fit.
the court calculates in the ways that the astronomers calculate. The orbit of the moon and its position relative to the sun.
to the north of the sun or to its south. That the place where the moon is seen may be north or south of the place where the sun sets (for this calculation see below 16:10).
and whether it was wide or narrow. Whether the crescent that will be seen is thick or thin (for this calculation see below 18:3).
and where the tips of its horns incline. To which direction the tips of the crescent face (for this calculation see below 19:1-14).
how high it was. Above the western horizon (for this calculation see below 19:15).
they correspond to what was known by calculation. They match the calculation the court made.
they accept them. And sanctify the month on their testimony.
we saw it in the water. Its reflection in water.
in the clouds. Through the clouds.
in a glass. Through glass (and Meiri, Rosh Hashanah 24a, explained that they saw its reflection in a glass vessel).
this is not a sighting. Since the moon itself was not seen clearly.
about two heights. Twice the height of a person.
and the second said it was about three heights high, they join. For it is likely that one of them erred in estimating this measure (for a similar halacha see Hilchot Edut 2:4-5).
and each of them joins with a second who testifies as he does. Each of them is fit to join with another witness who testifies as he does.
or the difference between them is one height. The difference between them will be only one height.
they said, 'we saw it without intention'. Without having intended to come to testify.
lest clouds knotted together and appeared like the moon. See above 1:6.

'We saw it on the morning of the twenty-ninth in the east... and we saw it in the evening in the west on the night of the thirtieth'. This is an impossible reality, for it cannot be that the interval between the moon's disappearance and its first sighting is only twelve hours (see above 1:3).
for we are not responsible for the morning sighting. The court deals only with testimony about the sighting of the birth of the moon, and other matters are not its concern.
they saw it at its time. On the night of the thirtieth, at the time when by calculation it could have been seen, and this testimony was confirmed.
and on the night of its intercalation. The night of the thirty-first (above 1:4).
for we are responsible only for the sighting of the night of the thirtieth alone. For the sighting of the birth of the moon at its time, and not for its sighting or absence on other days.
in the examinations that we mentioned. Above, halacha 4.
the great one. The important one.
his words were found to correspond to the calculation. They correspond to the reality expected according to the astronomical calculation.
their words were found to correspond. They match one another.
the main points. The essentials of the matter in brief.
not that they need them. For the testimony of the first ones was already accepted.
so that they do not leave dejected. Disappointed that they took the trouble and came for nothing.
so that they will be accustomed to come. Perhaps on another occasion they will be the only witnesses who can testify.
after the testimony is established. Examined and accepted.
with three. In a panel of three ordained judges (below 5:1).

and we sanctify only a month that was seen at its time. On the night of the thirtieth, and not if it was seen on the night of the thirty-first, for 'we do not attend to the moon on the night of the thirty-first, whether it was seen or not' (above 1:3).
and we sanctify only by day. For the sanctification of the month is like a trial, which is held only by day (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 3:3).
the court and all Israel saw it. The moon at its renewal, so that the matter became publicly known.
until dark. Night fell and the stars came out (below, halacha 9).
the court itself saw it. The judges who determine the month.
at the end of the twenty-ninth day. Before the emergence of the stars.
the court says. Without needing to receive testimony, since the sighting of the moon takes the place of testimony.
for it is still day. Until the emergence of the stars.
the next day they seat two judges etc.. When they sanctify it by day, they cannot rely on the moon they saw at night, which is no longer before them, but must testify about it themselves.
those who erred. Who erred on their own.
those who were misled. Who were misled by others.
those who were coerced. Who were forced by others to sanctify the month.
to fix the festivals on the day on which they sanctified. To establish the festivals according to the date that was fixed.
for this one knew that they erred. For example, one person calculated and knows by calculation that it is impossible for the moon to have been seen.
'which you shall proclaim them'. For the Torah explicitly taught that the matter depends on the proclamation and enactment of the court alone.
who saw the month. The first sighting of the moon.
the court. The court in charge of sanctifying the month (see below 5:1).

a journey of a night and a day. A walking distance of a full day, so that if they set out immediately after sighting the moon at the beginning of the night, they can reach the court before the end of the next day, and the court will sanctify the month on their testimony.
is effective. Is of use.
even if it was Shabbat. And they will have to desecrate Shabbat to make this journey.
as it is said. In the Torah's command concerning the festivals.
and wherever it says 'mo'ed' it overrides Shabbat. For the word 'mo'ed' indicates that this matter belongs specifically to a designated time (see also Hilchot Korban Pesach 1:18).

therefore one desecrates only... for the sake of the establishment of the festivals. Because desecrating Shabbat was permitted only in connection with the observance of the festivals, one desecrates it only for those months in which festivals fall.

because of the additional offering of every Rosh Chodesh, which overrides Shabbat. Since the offering overrides Shabbat (see Hilchot Bi'at Mikdash 4:10), the determination that causes it to be offered likewise overrides Shabbat.
the witnesses who vouch for them to the court. Who testify about the witnesses who saw the moon, that they are fit (above 2:3).
goes with them. With the witnesses who go to testify about the month.
lest another be found. That perhaps an additional witness who knows the witnesses will be found, so that his arrival will be needed.
even on a bed. He can be carried on it.
an ambusher. An enemy who may attack them on the way.
weapons. Arms, even though all this involves additional desecration of Shabbat.
even if they saw it large and visible to all. Even if the renewal of the moon was clearly visible, and it is to be assumed that others saw it too.
and he is fit to testify. As explained above 2:1.
it is a mitzvah for him to desecrate Shabbat, go and testify. Lest he be needed for the testimony about the month.
at first. In the early days.
the whole of the thirtieth day. Throughout the day.
were delayed. Were held up.
between the evenings. The time of the afternoon daily offering, after which no other offerings are brought (Hilchot Temidin UMusafin 1:3).
and they were disrupted in the Temple. They encountered a problem that disrupted the usual order.
the musaf of the day. The additional offering of Rosh Chodesh.
until the afternoon prayer time. Which is about two and a half hours before nightfall.
and their libations. Additions of a wine libation and a meal offering of fine flour mixed with oil, which were brought on the altar with most of the offerings.
they bring the afternoon daily offering. They slaughter and offer it.

they observe it that day as holy and the next day as holy. From the beginning of the thirtieth day, on which they await witnesses, they observed the sanctity of Rosh Chodesh, in case witnesses would come and the month would be sanctified. And even when it is known that they will not sanctify it but it will be postponed to the next day, they continue to observe its sanctity (and similarly they did with Rosh Hashanah, as explained below 5:8).
that they did not sanctify it. The thirtieth day.
after the Temple was destroyed. And since the daily offering is no longer offered, the reason for the enactment was nullified.
close to sunset. When enough time remains for examining the witnesses and sanctifying the month before the stars emerge (above 2:7-9).
because no witnesses came the whole of the thirtieth day. Above 1:6.
to a prepared place. A place designated for this purpose, such as a synagogue (see Meiri, Sanhedrin 70b).
and they make a feast there. So that it becomes publicly known that they intercalated the month.
but at dusk. They rise early before dawn, so that the matter becomes known.
with grain bread and legumes. Bread and a dish of legumes.
the mitzvah meal of intercalating the month mentioned everywhere. In all sources that mention the mitzvah meal of intercalating the month, this meal is meant (and see below 18:9).

they would light beacons on the tops of the mountains. On the night of the thirty-first they light torches and signal with them quickly from mountain to mountain, thus conveying to all Israel the news that the month was sanctified (and if they did not sanctify the month, because the moon was not seen at its time, they did not light beacons at all, and thus people knew that the month was intercalated).
after the Kutim corrupted. The Samaritans. Because they were in conflict with the Jews, they wished to disrupt their arrangements.
to establish it. To publicize the date of the sanctification of the month.
and for Av because of the fast. Tisha B'Av, which they fasted on even in the time of the Temple (Commentary on the Mishnah, Rosh Hashanah 1:3).
that they sit and wait on the thirtieth of Elul. Since it is possible that this day will be fixed as Rosh Hashanah.
if they learned that the court had sanctified the thirtieth day etc.. For example, those who live in a place near the court.
until the messengers of Tishrei come to them. And inform them when the month was sanctified.
the establishment of the festivals. To fix the rest of the festivals in it: Yom Kippur and the festival of Sukkot.
Pesach Katan. The Second Passover.

the messengers of Nisan and the messengers of Tishrei etc.. Because of the enactment of the festivals that fall in these months, they do not rely on estimates and conjecture, but wait until the court says 'mekudash' and Rosh Chodesh is clearly fixed (see above 2:8).

at the end of the twenty-ninth day, as we said. Above 2:9, that it is possible that the moon was seen before the end of the twenty-ninth day of the month, and the court managed to sanctify it that same day.
they go out from the evening. On the night of Rosh Chodesh.
the other six months. The remaining months of the six enumerated in the previous halacha.
since the month was seen etc.. And they can rely on the assumption that the court will sanctify it the next day.
that the messengers would arrive. Before the festival.
they would observe two days because of the doubt etc.. See also below 5:4-12.
and the messengers of Tishrei did not reach them. See the next halacha.
so as not to divide the festivals. Not to divide their laws and make some of them one day and some two days.
for any place that the messengers of Tishrei did not reach. Which is a distance of more than ten days from Jerusalem (below 5:11).

even the festival of Atzeret. The festival of Shavuot, whose time is fifty days after the first day of Passover (Hilchot Temidin UMusafin 8:1), and whose date depends on the determination of Rosh Chodesh Nisan. Although there is ample time to notify them of it, they enacted that this too be observed for two days in places that the messengers of Tishrei do not reach.
and how far is it between the messengers of Nisan and the messengers of Tishrei. What is the difference between the traveling time of the messengers of Nisan and that of the messengers of Tishrei.

because it is a festival etc.. Of Rosh Hashanah, and it is forbidden to go out on it and on Yom Kippur beyond the Shabbat limit of two thousand cubits (Hilchot Eruvin 8:4), and therefore they will be delayed on the way.
that they be two. As is the law for witnesses.
and not a single messenger. Specially appointed by the court.
a merchant. A trader.
and they fix the festivals. They set the date of the festivals.

a matter that is destined to be revealed. And since this matter is going to become known, there is no concern that the witness is lying (and see also Hilchot Gerushin 12:15, Hilchot Yibbum VaChalitzah 4:31).
that they sat the whole of the thirtieth day. During the time that sighting the moon is possible by calculation (as explained above 1:6).
as we explained in this chapter. Above, halacha 7.
distant witnesses. From a faraway place.
the night of the thirtieth. Of the previous month.
they threaten them with a great threat. With questions and examinations.
and confuse them. Bewilder them.
and burden them with examinations and scrutinize their testimony. They press them with many questions and about the details of the testimony.
since its name has gone out as intercalated. Since it was already decided to intercalate it and the matter was publicized.
the witnesses stood by their testimony. They were precise about the details of the testimony in accordance with the court's calculations, despite the efforts to trip them up.
and it was found to be consistent. The accounts of the two witnesses match each other.

and the witnesses are well-known and wise men. Prominent people and Torah scholars whose purpose in testifying is for the sake of Heaven. It may also be explained that because the witnesses are known and wise, their honor must not be slighted (Yad Peshutah).
they sanctify it and count that month again from the thirtieth day. They sanctify the month retroactively from the day of the sighting, and move the date back by one day.
since the moon was seen on its night. At the time it was expected to be seen, and the matter was established beyond any doubt.

and if the court needed to leave this month intercalated as it was before these witnesses came. To leave it as intercalated as it was before the witnesses came. For sometimes months are intercalated and shortened by calculation, to preserve the average of the months (below 18:5-11).
they leave it. They leave the earlier determination in place, and do not accept the witnesses at all.
and this is what they said: we intercalate the month for a need. Even if it later became clear that the moon was seen at its time.
and some of the great Sages. Among the Sages of the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 20a).
and we do not threaten them. To trip them up with questions and examinations, so that this does not look like falsehood.
for the dispute of the Sages is not in this matter. Brought in the previous halacha.
but in the other months. In which the intercalation of the month does not affect the determination of the festivals.
they accept their testimony. And they fix the time of the festivals according to it.

whose testimony was flawed etc.. That they erred in their words, and their testimony did not exactly match the court's calculations, or one did not match the other. And if the testimony is not accepted, Rosh Chodesh will be postponed to the next day, even though by calculation the moon should have been seen.
they threaten them so that the testimony will be established and it will be sanctified at its time. They press them to be more precise in their words so that their testimony will be accepted.
witnesses came to refute the witnesses... before the court sanctified it. And after the sanctification of the month, no attention is paid to the refuting witnesses at all (above 2:10).
it is the year in which a month is added. To make up the gap between the solar year and the lunar year (above 1:2).

and we never add except Adar. Which is the month adjacent to the season of the spring. Moreover, it is the last month of the biblical year (similar to the intercalation of a month, which is done at the end of the month; see Mechilta, Bo, chapter 2).

the season of Aviv. The spring season between the days of the sun and the rainy season, when the grain begins to ripen (Yad Peshutah). Some explain that it refers to the tekufah of Nisan, that is, the equinox, as explained in the next halacha (Shekel HaKodesh).

'Observe the month of Aviv' etc.. The continuation of the verse: 'and keep the Passover to the Lord your God,' from which we learn that one must be careful about the timing of the month so that the festival of Passover falls in the spring season.

sometimes in the days of the sun and sometimes in the rainy days. Since the lunar year is shorter than the solar year, the accumulating gap would cause the months to fall in different seasons of the year (as in the Muslim calendar).

on three signs they intercalate the year. Three different indications that the spring season has not yet arrived (Yad Peshutah; according to Shekel HaKodesh, mentioned above, these are not signs of the spring season but three separate reasons).
on the tekufah, on the aviv, and on the fruits of the tree. These three signs will be explained shortly.
the tekufah of Nisan. The spring equinox (for the methods of calculating the tekufah see below chapters 9-10, and especially below 10:6).
and we do not worry about another sign. There is no need to check the other signs (see the next halacha).
the aviv. Barley, which is the first grain to ripen.
it is late. It is slow to ripen.
they rely on these two signs. If both appeared.
so that the aviv will be available to offer the omer wave offering from it. For barley is needed for the omer offering, whose time is the sixteenth of Nisan (Hilchot Temidin UMusafin 7:3 ff.).
and so that the fruits will grow as is usual in the whole season of aviv. For one of the characteristics of the spring season is the growth of fruits.
three lands. Three districts in the Land of Israel (this division is used for other matters too; see Hilchot Ishut 13:16, Hilchot Shemittah 7:9).
they rely on the aviv. For the purpose of checking whether the barley has already ripened.

which are the main ones... for the years to be solar years. The tekufah, the aviv and the fruits are the reasons that stem directly from the need to align the months with the seasons of the year (and there are other reasons detailed below).
because of the need. Of many Israelites for the pilgrimage and for celebrating Passover in Jerusalem, although these reasons are not needed in terms of aligning Nisan with the spring season.
the roads that are not repaired. That were ruined by the rains and are not easy to travel.
to go up. On pilgrimage for the festival of Passover.

they block and prevent the people, or they endanger themselves and die. They block passage for the public, or alternatively people endanger themselves by crossing the river and are eventually swept away and die.
the ovens of the Passover offerings that were lost in the rains. For the ovens in which the Passover offering was roasted were made of clay, and are ruined by heavy rains.
and they will dry. They will dry and be ready for roasting the Passover offering.

the exiles of Israel who were uprooted from their places and have not yet reached Jerusalem. Diaspora residents who set out toward Jerusalem but were delayed and will not manage to arrive by Passover.
but they do not intercalate... because of the cold. The cold, which does not prevent celebrating the festival.
nor because of the exiles of Israel who have not yet been uprooted from their places. Who have not yet set out for Jerusalem.

nor because of impurity etc.. For although one may not offer in a state of impurity (see Hilchot Bi'at Mikdash 4:1), the Passover offering has a special law that if most of the community or of the priests are impure through contact with the dead, they perform it in impurity (Hilchot Korban Pesach 7:1, Hilchot Bi'at Mikdash 4:12); therefore the year is not intercalated in order to do it in purity.
and if they intercalated the year because of impurity, it is intercalated. But not for the other reasons.
support for a year that needs intercalation. Help and reinforcement for the need to intercalate the year, as explained in the next halacha.
for they are few. There is a small number of them.
the young pigeons that have not yet flown. Young doves that have not grown feathers.
the kids and lambs are available for the Passover offerings. For the Passover offering, for which only kids and lambs up to one year of age are fit (Hilchot Korban Pesach 1:1).
for the appearance offering. The offering of appearance, since every person must bring a burnt offering to the Temple when going up for the pilgrimage (Hilchot Chagigah 1:1).
they say, 'This year needs intercalation' etc.. So they write in the letters sent by the Nasi to all Israel (below, halacha 17).
the tekufah that was prolonged. The tekufah of Tevet, which was prolonged and will not end before Passover.
and also the kids are small and the young pigeons are tender. And by intercalating the year this problem too will be solved.
those designated for it. Who were specially invited to come to the deliberation on intercalating the year, and seven judges are invited in advance (below, halacha 10).
the head of the Great Court. The Nasi of the Great Sanhedrin of seventy-one (below, halacha 10; Hilchot Sanhedrin 1:3).
they begin with three. To determine whether there is a need to deliberate on intercalating the year.
from those who were ordained. Who were ordained as judges as explained in Hilchot Sanhedrin chapter 4, for the year is intercalated only by ordained judges (ibid. 5:7, and see below 5:1).
we need not sit and we need not look. There is no need for this examination.
the one is nullified by the minority. Against the other two, and it was decided that there is no need to deliberate on intercalation.
and they deliberate in a panel of five. In a panel of five.
two were nullified by their minority. Relative to the three, and it was decided that they do not intercalate it that year.
and they deliberate and conclude with seven. Because of the importance of intercalating the year (see also Hilchot Sanhedrin 5:7).
they concluded. They decided.
or who will agree. Who will consent to the determination of the intercalation, even though he did not take part in the deliberations (see also below, halacha 12).

and in intercalating the year they begin from the side etc.. They give permission to speak first to the youngest of the judges, whose seat is at the edge (see Hilchot Sanhedrin 10:6), and he is also the one who announces the intercalation of the year (Jerusalem Talmud, Rosh Hashanah 2:5).
and for sanctifying the month they begin from the greatest. The head of the court, who is the one who announces the sanctification of the month (above 2:8).
they do not seat for the intercalation of the year. Among the judges who deliberate on intercalating the year.
lest his mind incline. That he may incline in his opinion and decide the intercalation issue because of a benefit he has in the matter.
because of the cold etc.. For if the year is intercalated, Yom Kippur will be delayed to the cold days, and the water in which he immerses will be cold.
five immersions. As explained in Hilchot Avodat Yom HaKippurim 2:2-3.
on a distant road. And cannot join the deliberations on intercalation.
in the land of Judah, in which the Divine Presence dwells. In the territory of the tribe of Judah, within whose boundaries Jerusalem and the site of the Temple lie.

'to His dwelling you shall seek'. And they derived from this that next to the place of the Lord ('His dwelling'), that is, in the land of Judah adjacent to Jerusalem, there matters of halacha are to be deliberated ('you shall seek').
and we intercalate only by day. Like the sanctification of the month, as explained above 2:8.
the court may. They are permitted.
they do not say, 'such-and-such year is intercalated'. They do not announce the intercalation of the year publicly.
and this is because of pressing circumstances. This permission applies only when they will not be able to say it at a later time.

it is in Adar that they say it. This is the proper time to announce the intercalation ideally, for then they used to intercalate the year, since they can see whether there is a need for it because of the aviv, the fruits and the like (Yad Ramah, Sanhedrin 12a, and as above, halachot 3-8). Also, if they announce too early, the intercalation may be forgotten, and this could lead to the mishap of eating chametz on Passover (Rashi, Sanhedrin 12a).
for that day is fit to be Rosh Chodesh Nisan. If sighting is possible and witnesses come.
and if they intercalated it on the thirtieth of Adar, it is intercalated etc.. Since as long as they have not sanctified the month, it is still the month of Adar.
in a year of famine. When grain is not available.
for everyone is running to the threshing floors to eat and live. They are hard pressed and awaiting the eating of the crop of the new year, which is in the grain storehouses.

and it is impossible to add time for them to the prohibition of the new grain. For it is forbidden to harvest and eat the grain of the new crop until after the omer meal offering is brought on the sixteenth of Nisan (Hilchot Temidin UMusafin 7:13, Hilchot Ma'achalot Asurot 10:2). And if a month is added to the year, the time of permission would be postponed by another month.
and we do not intercalate in the Sabbatical year. In the Sabbatical year, in which it is forbidden to work and sow the fields.

for everyone's hand is free to take the aftergrowth. The grain that grows by itself in the Sabbatical year ('sefichin') is ownerless and open to all, and if the time of the offering is postponed, there may not be enough left of it for the offering.
and they used to intercalate on the eve of the Sabbatical year. To add time for working the land before the Sabbatical year (Rashi, Sanhedrin 12a).
because of the need. Of celebrating Passover in Jerusalem, as explained above, halacha 5.
fit to be intercalated etc.. As explained above, halachot 2-4.
they intercalate always at any time. Since there is a command to celebrate Passover in the spring season (above, halacha 1), these considerations are not sufficient to postpone it.
and why. For what reason.
and in the name of the Nasi. In his name.

they wanted... for the distant people whom they inform. The court calculates whether the additional month will be full or deficient, and according to their calculation they write in the letters they send to distant places.

but they act according to the sighting. For the actual determination of the month is made by sighting, and therefore one must wait for the day of Rosh Chodesh itself, and their announcement in these letters is not sufficient to fix the month (Yad Peshutah).
all that we have said about fixing Rosh Chodesh by sighting. In chapters 1-3.
and the intercalation of the year because of the season or because of need. In chapter 4.
the Sanhedrin in the Land of Israel. Which numbers seventy-one sages.
an ordained court. Whose judges were appointed for halachic rulings (for the manner of ordination see Hilchot Sanhedrin 4:1).
and from oral tradition. A halachic tradition.
and for everyone who stands after them in their place. For the Nasi of the Sanhedrin fills the place of Moses our teacher (see ibid. 1:3).
except by this calculation that we calculate by today. The method of calculation is explained below in chapters 6-10 (and see also below 11:4).
and we do not attend to sighting. When fixing by calculation, the actual sighting of the moon is not taken into account.
but sometimes it will be etc.. Sometimes Rosh Chodesh falls on the very day of sighting, but sometimes it is fixed a day before or after the time of sighting the moon.
it is a wonder. It happens on rare occasions.

and in the lands west of the Land of Israel. Where sunset is later, and the moon may be seen a day before the determination of Rosh Chodesh. Because the renewal of the moon can be seen only close to sunset, and by the time sunset reaches these lands, the moon will have moved and distanced itself from the sun, and its light will have grown in the meantime (see also below 18:13).
and from when. From what period. [Note: Rambam vocalizes this word in the Commentary on the Mishnah as 'amatai'.]
until the days of Abaye and Rava. Who lived in Babylonia until the middle of the fourth century CE.
on the determination of the Land of Israel. The determination of the Sages of the Land of Israel, who sanctified according to sighting.
and all the places that the messengers of Tishrei reach etc.. This halacha is explained above 3:11-13.
in this time when there is no Sanhedrin there. When the Sanhedrin does not exist (see Rambam's introduction to the Mishneh Torah, section 30).

it would be proper for all places to observe one festival day... for all rely and fix on one calculation. For today there is no doubt about when the festival falls, since everywhere they rely on the same calculation.
that they should be careful with the custom of their fathers in their hands. And they should continue to observe two festival days even in this time.
therefore. Because the Sages enacted that they be careful with the ancient custom.
any place that the messengers of Tishrei did not reach. Which were defined as distant places (above, halacha 4).
they observe one day, as is their custom, for they never observed two days. And they have no 'custom of the fathers' to celebrate two days.
it turns out that the second festival day is of rabbinic origin. The enactment of the Sages to preserve it, and not because of the doubt (see also Hilchot Yom Tov 1:21).
the festival day of Rosh Hashanah. That fell on Rosh Chodesh itself.

most of the people of the Land of Israel observed it for two days because of doubt. For most people of the land (apart from those within the Jerusalem area) could not know on that day whether the month had been sanctified or intercalated, and therefore they celebrated Rosh Hashanah on both days (above 3:9).
since the messengers do not go out on a festival. For the sanctity of the festival is not desecrated in order to announce the intercalation (above 3:8).

for if witnesses did not come the whole of the thirtieth day, they observed on that day on which they awaited witnesses it as holy and the next day as holy. That when it was possible that the moon was seen on the night of the thirtieth, they awaited the witnesses the next day, and observed this day from its beginning as a festival, since if the witnesses came that day, it would be fixed that this day is Rosh Hashanah. But if no witnesses came all day, the next day was fixed as Rosh Hashanah, and then Rosh Hashanah was celebrated for two days (see above 3:5-7).
that even the people of the Land of Israel always observe it for two days. For so was the custom of their fathers.

behold you have learned that even the second festival day of Rosh Hashanah in this time is of rabbinic origin. And it is not because of the doubt, but because of the custom. Nevertheless there are differences between the sanctity of the second day of Rosh Hashanah and that of other festival days (see Hilchot Yom Tov 1:24).
that they are obligated to observe two days. For when there was no custom in that place, we follow the custom of most of the world, as explained below, halacha 12.

or because there was a danger on the road etc.. That the road was dangerous, for at that time the Kutim of Samaria were hostile to the Jews and did not allow free passage between Judah and the Galilee. So it turns out that even at the time when the month was fixed by sighting, it was necessary in that place to observe two festival days because of doubt.
the observance of one day does not depend on the proximity of the place. According to its distance from Jerusalem.
for who will tell us that messengers went out to this place. For there are nearby places that the messengers did not reach for various reasons, as follows.
and after they returned to fix by the calculation, Israelites settled there. After they began to rely on the calculation accepted in our days, Jews settled there.
all the people of Egypt observed one day. And in practice they used to observe two days.
by the way of Ashkelon. The coastal road, which is the short way to Egypt.

Syria. A region corresponding mostly to the state of Syria, northeast of the Land of Israel (which in some matters has the law of the Land of Israel and in others that of the Diaspora; Hilchot Terumot 1:3).
a journey of more than ten full days. A distant place that requires more than ten full days of travel to reach.
according to their custom from before. For so they did when the month was sanctified by sighting (above 3:12).

for the messengers of each and every Tishrei reach only a place that is ten days or less from Jerusalem. In some years there are two Shabbatot between Rosh Hashanah and the festival of Sukkot, and after deducting the Shabbatot, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur (on which it is forbidden to go beyond the Shabbat limit), only ten weekdays remain on which the messengers may travel (see above 3:12-13).

if that place is part of the Land of Israel in which Israelites lived at the time of sighting, in the Second Conquest. In places known to have been inhabited by Jews in the time of the return to Zion, when they sanctified the month by sighting. [Note: In the Commentary on the Mishnah Rambam vocalizes the name of the city Tiberias as 'Teverya'.]
and if that place is from Syria etc.. Places adjacent to the Land of Israel on the north.
and Ashkelon. Also adjacent to the Land of Israel and bounding it on the south.
or from outside the land, such as Egypt etc.. The countries more distant from the Land of Israel.
they act according to the custom of their fathers in their hands. As they did in the time of sanctifying the month by sighting.
if one day, one day; and if two days, two days. Everything as they observed in that place, depending on whether the messengers reached it.
and they have no custom. Since it is not known how they behaved there in ancient times.
or a city that was newly founded in the desert of the Land of Israel. A city built in a place that was previously uninhabited.
or a place where Israelites dwell now. A place where only gentiles lived in the past, and a Jewish community settled there after the transition to fixing the calendar by calculation.
and every second festival day is of rabbinic origin. As explained above, halacha 6.
for everyone observes it in this time. Even the people of the Land of Israel, as explained above, halacha 8.
for we do not intercalate years or fix months outside the Land. Above 1:8.
and we rely only on the calculation of the people of the Land of Israel and their determination. For the Sages of the Land of Israel calculate in this way, and fix the festivals accordingly.
to reveal the matter. To know when Rosh Chodesh will fall according to the calculation of the people of the Land of Israel.
when they act according to sighting. As explained above in chapters 1-3.
the hour at which the moon gathers with the sun. The time at which the moon passes in front of the sun, which is the starting point of the cycle.
with great precision. Exactly.
the astronomers. The astronomers who watch the stars and calculate their movements.
to know whether the moon will be seen or not. See above 1:6.
and the beginning of that calculation. The first stage in arriving at the exact calculation.
is a calculation that is made approximately. On average, and afterward corrections and adjustments are made on it in order to arrive at the exact calculation.
by their mean motion. By an averaged calculation.
molad. So called because it is the time of the moon's birth (by the mean calculation).
and it is the calculation that we calculate today. By which months are fixed and years intercalated (above 5:1).
twenty-four hours at all times. Equal hours (as we measure today, as opposed to the seasonal hours used in other contexts in halacha).

twelve in the day and twelve in the night. For the division is made by an average day and night of twelve equal hours, where the time of the beginning of day and night is fixed by the average of the times of sunrise and sunset, and the counting of the hours of the day begins at the start of the night.
chalakim (parts). The duration of each part is 3 and 1/3 seconds (18 parts to a minute).
it has etc.. It can be divided into all these parts without remainder.
and an eighth. One eighth.
and a sixth. One sixth.
and a ninth. One ninth.
and a tenth. One tenth.
and many parts are named by all these names. For each of the fractions listed can be divided into many secondary divisions.
by their mean motion. In the mean calculation, as above, halacha 1.

and this is the month of the moon. The mean duration of a 'lunar month' (although for calculating the calendar they fix months of whole days, sometimes twenty-nine days and sometimes thirty; see below 8:1-3).
its total will be. Its whole sum.
and the solar year. The time it takes the sun to return to the same point on the plane of the ecliptic (an imaginary circle on which the sun is observed as if circling during the year).

three hundred sixty-five days and six hours. Below 9:1 it is explained that this is the calculation according to some of the Sages, and there is another, more precise, calculation (see below 10:1, 10:6).
it turns out that the excess of the solar year over the lunar year. The difference between the solar year and the lunar year.

when you discard etc.. In order to focus the calculation on finding the day of the week and the hour at which the molad will fall in the next month, one can ignore the whole weeks that will pass and consider only the remainder of days and hours, as illustrated below in halachot 6-7.

their mnemonic is alef-yod-bet, tav-shin-tzadi-gimmel. The first letter indicates the days, the letters after it the hours, and after them the number of parts is given (that is, 1 day, 12 hours, 793 parts).
and this is the remainder of the lunar month. The time difference between the day of the week on which the previous molad fell and the day on which the next molad falls.
on Sunday. The first day of the week.
the remainder of the lunar month, which is alef-yod-bet, tav-shin-tzadi-gimmel. As explained above, halacha 5.

the molad of Iyar will come out on the night of Tuesday, five hours into the night and nine hundred parts. By adding one day to Sunday, on which the molad of Nisan fell, we reach Monday. By adding 12 hours to the 17 hours of the day of the molad of Nisan we reach the fifth hour of Monday night (the night of Tuesday), and the addition of the parts accumulates to 900 parts.
and in this way until the end of the world. In this manner one can continue to calculate the time of the molad of each and every month without limit.
month after month. This is how one calculates by adding a single month, and below the way to calculate larger units will be explained.
the molad of this year. The molad of the month of Tishrei, with which the year begins (below, halacha 13).
and the first molad from which you begin. Which is considered the starting point of our calculation.

in the first year of creation. The year of the creation of the world (which is the count of years we use today), and the number of years that have passed since then is used as the basis for all the calculations (as explained below in halachot 13-14).

when you add remainder to remainder. You will combine the remainder in excess of a whole week of one month with the remainder of a second month (as explained above in halachot 6-7), or the remainder of one year with that of a second year (above, halacha 8), and likewise the remainder of one cycle with that of a second cycle, as explained below in halachot 12-13.

every nineteen years... is called a machzor (cycle). Since for calculating the molad there is a difference between simple and leap years, one must know the order in which simple and leap years are fixed, which is called a 'machzor'. Using this unit makes it possible to calculate the molads over periods of nineteen years.
of which seven years are leap years and twelve are simple. According to the order explained in the next halacha.
and why did we rely on this count. Why is it necessary to create a cycle of 19 years.

and nothing will remain of the count of the solar days in the whole of nineteen years except one hour etc.. So that there is an almost complete correspondence between solar years and lunar years (and see below 9:1 and 10:6, that according to the view of the Sages which we follow in practice in calculating the calendar, the correspondence is complete with no remainder at all).
the months are all lunar months and the years solar years. For in such a structure the lunar months add up to 19 whole solar years.

and the seven leap years in each and every cycle. Such a distribution of the leap years (once every two or three years) is meant to prevent the accumulation of too large a gap between the solar year and the lunar year.
when the remainder is gathered. When you add the remainders of the molads of the simple and leap years of the cycle, in the manner described above, halacha 9.
and add to it bet-yod-vav, tav-kuf-tzadi-heh. Which is the remainder of the cycle (that is, 2 days, 16 hours, 595 parts).
and we have already said. Above, halacha 8.

and the molad of the year is the molad of Tishrei of that year. This refers to the molad of the month of Tishrei at its beginning, by which the dates of the year are fixed (taking into account the postponements below in chapter 7).
years of creation. Which is the count of years used in the Hebrew date.
and make them cycles etc.. One divides by 19 and takes the remainder into account.
and for every simple year etc.. As detailed above, halacha 8.
and gather everything and complete the parts into hours etc.. In the manner explained above, halacha 10.
and discard the days seven by seven. To find the day of the week on which the molad falls.
that comes out in this calculation. After the calculations in halacha 14.
and when you add to it etc.. As explained above (halacha 5), the addition of the remainder of one month.
Rosh Chodesh Tishrei is never fixed etc.. This chapter explains how Rosh Chodesh Tishrei is fixed, according to which the other months of the year are fixed, as will be explained in chapter 8.
according to this calculation. The calculation by which the intercalation of months and years is fixed in the time when there is no Sanhedrin (above 5:2).
their mnemonic is alef-dalet-vav. Sunday, Wednesday and Friday.
when the molad of Tishrei is. According to the mean calculation as explained in chapter 6.
they fix Rosh Chodesh on the day after it. The reason for this postponement appears below, halachot 7-8.
if the molad is. The molad of the month of Tishrei according to the mean calculation.
at midday or above midday. At noon, which is the sixth hour, or after it.
they fix Rosh Chodesh on the following day. This postponement is called 'molad zaken' (Tur).
and if the molad was before midday even by one part. Even if the molad precedes midday by a small amount, which is one part of one thousand and eighty to the hour (above 6:2).
that that day should not be one of the days alef-dalet-vav. As explained above, halacha 1.
when the molad is. Of the month of Tishrei.
at midday or after midday, and it is postponed to the following day. As explained in the previous halacha.
on the third from the day of the molad. Two days after the day of the molad.
its mnemonic is zayin-yod-chet. Shabbat, at the sixth hour of the day, which is the eighteenth hour from the start of the day cycle (above 6:2).
in a year whose molad is like this. The molad of the year is the molad of Tishrei (above 6:13).
or more than this. And later on that same day.

if it is a simple year, they postpone Rosh Chodesh. For if the molad falls at this time, the molad of Tishrei in the following year (after adding the remainder of a simple year, explained above 6:5) will fall on Shabbat in the eighteenth hour (noon) or after it. Thus Rosh Hashanah will be postponed by two days, to Monday (as explained in the previous halacha). In this case it is necessary to postpone the day on which this Rosh Hashanah is fixed, so that the year will not be 356 days, a number greater than is possible according to the calendar (see below 8:7).

they do not fix Rosh Chodesh on Monday in this year but on Tuesday. For if the molad falls at this time, the molad of the previous year (calculated by subtracting the remainder of a leap year from the molad of this year, as above 6:4) fell on Tuesday in the eighteenth hour (noon) or after it. Thus the previous Rosh Hashanah was postponed by two days and fell on Thursday. In this case it is necessary to postpone the day on which this year is fixed, so that the previous year will not be 382 days, a number too small according to the calculation for a leap year (see below 8:8).
that we said it is postponed to Thursday. Above, halacha 4.
they fix it on Tuesday. Since the molad of the following year will fall on Shabbat before midday, there will be no need to postpone Rosh Hashanah.
they fix it on Monday. For the molad of the previous year fell on Tuesday before midday, and there was no need to postpone Rosh Hashanah.
you calculate and know the molad etc.. The mean molad, as explained above 6:6-14.
and the day of the molad is the day of fixing. And on it Rosh Hashanah falls.
in the way that we explained. Above, halachot 1-5.
for the gathering of the moon and the sun. The time at which the moon passes in front of the sun and begins a new cycle.
in their mean motion. On average.
as we informed. Above 6:1.
on Tuesday they fix etc.. In this way the gap between the average length of the month and the true length is balanced.
and the main reason. The cause.
the other four postponements. The three remaining postponements.
this is the main reason that we said. The explanation given in the previous halacha.
the moon will not be seen. The renewal of the moon will not be visible.

it follows that the sun and the moon did not truly gather until Thursday. For only about a day after the time of conjunction can the moon be seen (above 1:3). But in cases where the time of conjunction falls in the hours of the day, the actual sighting would be only after two days. And if the moon was not seen on the night of Friday, it is a sign that the time of conjunction did not precede Thursday.
the month of the moon. The mean cycle of the renewal of the moon.
as we explained. Above 6:3, that the length of the month is twenty-nine days, twelve hours and 793 parts.
and it is impossible to say that Rosh Chodesh will be for part of the day etc.. It is impossible to begin the month in the middle of the day, from the time of the molad onward.
from oral tradition. A halachic tradition in the exposition of the verses.
that you count days for the month and do not count hours. The month is composed of units of whole days, and it is impossible that a number of hours of the day should belong to a different month.
therefore. Because a month contains only whole days, and the length of the lunar cycle is between twenty-nine and thirty days.
so as not to count hours in the month but whole days. In this way the months can be fitted to the lunar cycle, as will be explained shortly.
twenty-nine and a half only. Without the addition of the parts of an hour.

but because of the parts... hours and days will accumulate from them etc.. Over time the parts in excess of the hour will accumulate into hours and even days, and this addition must be taken into account and the full and deficient months arranged so that there is correspondence between them and the lunar cycle.
by this calculation. Of fixing the calendar (not by sighting).
the month that has passed. The month that has just ended.
the thirtieth day will be Rosh Chodesh of the coming month. And it will be counted as the first day of the new month.

and if the month that passed was full, the thirtieth day will be Rosh Chodesh etc.. Although the thirtieth day is counted as the last day of the month that ended ('completion of the full month'), it is considered Rosh Chodesh for the prayers of the day and the like.
since part of it is Rosh Chodesh. For the lunar month is twenty-nine and a half days, so part of the thirtieth day is Rosh Chodesh, although the determination of the day is made the next day.
and the thirty-first day will be Rosh Chodesh of the coming month, and from it is the count. From it they begin to count the days of the new month.
and it is the day of fixing. This day is considered the day on which the month is fixed (for the calculation of months as explained in the rest of this chapter and in the previous one).
according to this calculation. But when sanctifying by sighting, the order may differ.
and the month of Tevet is always deficient. And the months Cheshvan and Kislev can vary, as explained shortly.
it is the one whose months are called full. And its length is three hundred fifty-five days in a simple year, and three hundred eighty-five days in a leap year.
its months are called deficient. And its length is three hundred fifty-three days in a simple year and three hundred eighty-three days in a leap year.
its months are called regular. And its length is three hundred fifty-four days in a simple year and three hundred eighty-four days in a leap year.
you first know the day on which Rosh Hashanah was fixed. On what day of the week Rosh Hashanah falls.
as we explained in chapter seven. According to the mean molad and the rules of postponement.

and calculate the number of days between them, apart from the day of fixing of this one and of that one. The difference between the day of the week on which the previous Rosh Hashanah falls and the day of the week of the next Rosh Hashanah, not including the days of Rosh Hashanah themselves.
if you find between them two days etc.. An illustration of this calculation is given below, halacha 9.
to know the arrangement of its months. Whether full, deficient or regular.
simple. Not a leap year.
that you can rely on them. That you can use them.
whose way we explained. Above chapter 7.

any year in which Rosh Hashanah is on Tuesday will always be regular etc.. For only the addition of three days (regular in a simple year) or five days (regular in a leap year) to Tuesday brings to a day on which the fixing of the next Rosh Hashanah is possible (Shabbat or Monday).

and if Rosh Hashanah is on Shabbat or Monday, it will never be regular. For adding three days to those days reaches Wednesday and Friday, and likewise adding five days to those days reaches Friday and Sunday, on which Rosh Hashanah is not fixed.
on Thursday, if it is simple, its months cannot be deficient. For if two days are added, we reach Sunday, on which it is not fixed.
and if it is a leap year, its months cannot be regular. For if five days are added we reach Wednesday, on which it is not fixed.
the solar year: some of the Sages of Israel etc.. The view of Shmuel the Sage (Eruvin 56a).

and there are those who say that it is less than a quarter of a day. This is the view of Rav Adda, which will be discussed at length in chapter 10, and according to which our calendar and the 19-year cycle were fixed (see especially below 10:6).
as we said. Above 6:10.
and between each tekufah and tekufah there will be. For there are four tekufot in the year (see the next halacha), and they divide the year into four equal parts.
until the end of the world. Forever, as far as you wish to calculate.

the tekufah of Nisan is the hour and part at which the sun enters the beginning of the constellation of Aries. The sun moves along a fixed path across the 'wheel of the constellations' that circles the world (see below 11:7-9), so that each month it is roughly in a different constellation, and it completes a full circuit every solar year (see also Hilchot Yesodei HaTorah 3:6-7). Around Nisan it reaches the beginning of Aries in its motion, and at that time day and night are equal in length (the spring equinox).
and the tekufah of Tammuz is the sun being at the head of the constellation of Cancer. The longest day of the year.
and the tekufah of Tishrei is the sun being at the head of the constellation of Libra. The autumn equinox.
and the tekufah of Tevet is the sun being at the head of the constellation of Capricorn. The shortest day of the year.
in the first year of creation. In which the world was created.
according to this calculation. Of a year length of three hundred sixty-five and a quarter days.
the way of calculating the tekufah. To know at what times the days of the tekufah fall; several methods of calculation are detailed below.

you first know how many cycles etc.. This is the basic calculation for finding the day of the month and the hour of the tekufah. This calculation is done by combining the remainders of the cycles from the time of the first tekufah and adding them to the molad of the month of Nisan at the beginning of the cycle in which one stands. From there on, a count of days and hours.
whole cycles. Each cycle is nineteen years, as explained above 6:10-11.

and take for each cycle of them etc.. For this is the accumulated excess of the solar years over the lunar years in each cycle (above 6:10), and therefore in each cycle the tekufah is postponed in this way relative to the molad of Nisan.

and gather all the parts into hours etc.. When one thousand and eighty parts have accumulated together with the remaining time of each cycle, they are converted to an hour, and when twenty-four hours have accumulated, they are converted to a day.
and subtract from the whole seven days, nine hours and six hundred forty-two parts. This is the time by which the first tekufah of Nisan preceded the molad of Nisan (above, halacha 3).
and the remainder. What remains from adding up the excess of the cycles after subtracting the time that preceded the first molad of Nisan.
add it to the molad of Nisan of the first year of the cycle. The method of calculating the molad is given in chapter 6.
and from it begin to count ninety-one days, seven and a half hours for each and every tekufah. And in this way one can find the times of all the tekufot in that cycle.

and if you wish to know the tekufah of Nisan of this year. In this calculation one arrives directly at the time of the tekufah of Nisan of that year, without counting days and hours from the beginning of the cycle, as in the previous paragraph.
take for all the whole cycles etc.. As explained in the previous paragraph.

and for all the complete years... ten days, twenty-one hours and two hundred four parts for each year. This is the excess of the solar year over the lunar year of twelve months (above 6:4), and therefore each year the tekufah is postponed in this way relative to the molad of Nisan.
and subtract from it seven days, nine hours and six hundred forty-two parts. As explained in the previous paragraph.

discard from them lunar months etc.. One must remove from the calculation the whole multiples of lunar months, since they were completed over the years by intercalating the year, and only the remainder is the difference that remains between the molad of Nisan and the tekufah.
the tekufah of Nisan according to this calculation. Which holds that the solar year is three hundred sixty-five and a quarter days.

is always only at the beginning of the night or at midnight or at the beginning of the day or at midday. Since the first tekufah of Nisan according to this calculation was at the beginning of the night, and each year it is postponed by exactly a quarter of a day, which is six hours.

and the tekufah of Tammuz is always only at seven and a half hours or at one and a half hours etc.. Since according to this calculation the time difference from one tekufah to the next is ninety-one days and seven and a half hours.

if you wish to know on what day of the week and at what hour the tekufah will be. This is a different calculation, by which one can calculate the day of the week and the hour at which the tekufah falls (and on its basis one can arrive at the date in the month, as explained below in halachot 6-7).

Introduction:. In the previous chapters it was explained how to calculate the place of the sun and the moon. On the basis of these calculations, this chapter explains how to calculate the chance of sighting the moon at the beginning of the thirtieth night of the month. This depends on two main factors: a) the size of the illuminated part of the moon; b) the time that will pass from sunset until moonset (the more time passes from sunset, the lower the intensity of sunlight and the greater the chances of sighting the moon). The size of the moon depends on its distance from the sun, called the 'first longitude' (below, halakhah 1), while the time of moonset is determined by the 'arc of sighting' (see diagram). According to the measure of the first longitude, and a preliminary estimate of the arc of sighting made according to the seasons of the year, one can make a preliminary assessment whether the moon will be seen or not (below, halakhot 3-4). In doubtful cases further calculations ('the sighting calculations') are needed to determine the arc of sighting more precisely (below, halakhot 5-15), and sometimes it is even necessary to carry out an additional calculation that weighs the relation between the visible size of the moon and the arc of sighting ('the limits of sighting' - below, halakhot 17-22).
